SpellcastingCharisma is the casting stat. Unlike a Wizard, the Sorcerer never prepares specific spells each morning — they cast spontaneously from a fixed Spells Known list, using whichever open slot fits, decided turn by turn. In exchange for that flexibility, the Sorcerer has fewer slots per day than a Wizard of the same level (see the Spell Progression table below). Spells Known are fixed until retrained during downtime.
CastingSpend a slot of the appropriate level to cast any spell from your Spells Known list — no roll required, no daily preparation. As with every caster, a higher-level slot can substitute for a lower-level spell with zero extra power (potency always scales by caster level, never by slot spent).
Bloodline KitAt character creation choose a Bloodline Kit. This defines your magical origin and grants a 1st-level Bloodline Ability and a 10th-level Bloodline Awakening.

Level by Level at a Glance

What you gain and when. Full details are under Class Abilities.

Class Abilities

1st Level

Spell Use

  • Effect: Cast spontaneously from your Spells Known list using any open slot of the right level. No preparation, no roll to succeed — casting works exactly like any other caster's slots.

Bloodline Ability

  • Effect: A benefit from your chosen Bloodline Kit. See the Bloodline Kits section.

Spellburn

  • Effect: Pay for Metamagic (see below) by sacrificing temporary points from Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution.
  • Spellburn never changes your HP or your death threshold, and burned points return at 1 per attribute each day.
  • Guaranteed, no roll, no Corruption risk.
  • The cost doubles with each Spellburn you make in a day: your first burn costs 1 point for the base effect, your second 2, your third 4, your fourth 8, and so on.
  • The enhanced effect costs double the base for that burn (2, then 4, then 8, then 16).
  • Unlike Wild Surge it has no daily limit, only what your body can afford.
  • Spellburn cannot reduce an attribute below 1. One Metamagic option per spell (two during Sorcerer's Spark)

Corruption

  • Effect: Whenever you choose the free route to Metamagic through Wild Surge (below) rather than paying with Spellburn, the GM rolls d20 in secret on the Corruption Table — a GM-only resource players never see.
  • A result of 1 triggers a Major Corruption event.
  • A result of 2-20 triggers a Minor Corruption effect — these can be cosmetic, beneficial, or detrimental.
  • The player knows something has shifted but not what the table said
  • Minor Corruption (GM only): a d20 result of 2–20.
d20Minor Corruption
2Colour drains from you: skin, hair and eyes turn ashen grey for 1 day. No other effect.
3Your shadow moves out of step with you for 1 hour. Disadvantage on Stealth checks for that time.
4Small loose objects within 5ft drift gently away from you for 1 hour. No other effect.
5A chill settles in your bones: Resistance 5 to cold damage for 1 hour.
6Your mouth fills with the taste of iron: Disadvantage on Persuasion checks for 1 hour.
7You crackle with static for 1 hour. The first creature to hit you with a melee attack takes 1d4 lightning damage.
8Dazzled: Disadvantage on Perception checks that rely on sight for 10 minutes.
9A flash of insight: Advantage on your next Intelligence or Wisdom check within 1 hour.
10You shed dim light in a 10ft radius for 1 hour. It cannot be dimmed or snuffed out.
11Frayed nerves: Disadvantage on your next Will save within 1 hour.
12Loose power shimmers about you: +1 AC for 1 hour.
13Animals within 30ft are agitated for 1 hour and will not willingly approach you.
14You can speak only in rhyme for 1 hour. No other effect.
15A surge of vigour: Advantage on your next Fortitude save within 1 hour.
16Your ears ring: you are Deafened for 1 minute.
17Your hair stands on end and crackles with sparks for 1 day. No other effect.
18A mild fever: Disadvantage on Fortitude saves for 1 hour.
19Your reflection refuses to match your movements for 1 day; mirrors and still water show something other than you. No other effect.
20The surge bleeds off harmlessly. No effect.
  • Major Corruption (GM only): on a result of 1, roll a d6.
d6Major Corruption
1Warped: part of you is permanently and visibly altered (scales, extra knuckles, a second pupil; the player and GM agree on the form). Disadvantage on Persuasion checks with strangers who notice it.
2Unravelling: you lose all unspent spell slots of your highest available level until your next full rest.
3Backlash: you take 1d6 force damage per level of the spell you cast (minimum 1d6).
4Wild echo: the spell is cast a second time at a random target or point within range, chosen by the GM.
5Stolen voice: you cannot speak for 24 hours and so cannot cast spells with verbal components.
6Rift: a hostile minor extraplanar creature (Level up to half your level, GM chooses) tears through within 30ft.

Metamagic Options

  • Effect: Choose one of the following each time you use Wild Surge or Spellburn. Wild Surge, or Spellburn at its base cost, gives the base effect; Spellburn at double the base cost gives the enhanced effect.
  • Twinned Spell: a spell that targets only one creature can target a second creature in range with the same casting; each is affected as normal. Enhanced: a third creature as well
  • Careful Spell: up to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1) creatures you choose automatically succeed on their save against the spell. Enhanced: they take no effect at all
  • Empowered Spell: reroll up to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1) damage dice and keep the new results. Enhanced: roll all the damage dice twice and keep the higher total
  • Extended Spell: double the duration. Enhanced: triple it, to a maximum of 24 hours
  • Heightened Spell: one target has Disadvantage on its first save against the spell. Enhanced: all targets do
  • Distant Spell: double the range; touch spells extend to 30ft. Enhanced: triple the range; touch extends to 60ft
  • Subtle Spell: cast with no somatic or verbal components. Enhanced: the casting also cannot be identified or counterspelled
  • Flexible Spell: freely change the damage type of the spell to any other type. Enhanced: it also ignores resistance to the new type
  • Quickened Spell: cast the spell and one cantrip with the same action; no other spell can be cast that turn. No enhanced effect. You may Quicken only one spell per round

2nd Level — Wild Surge

Wild Surge

  • Effect: Apply a Metamagic option's base effect to a spell for free instead of paying with Spellburn — but the GM rolls on the Corruption Table afterward.
  • This is the risky, free route to Metamagic.
  • Uses per day: 1 (2nd–8th level), 2 (9th–12th), 3 (13th–16th), 4 (17th–24th).
  • You may always pay with Spellburn instead to avoid the Corruption roll entirely

5th Level — Sorcerer's Spark

Sorcerer's Spark

  • Effect: Once per day, let the dam burst: for the encounter, any Wild Surge you use carries no Corruption risk, and you may apply two Metamagic options to a single spell simultaneously.

8th Level — Overchannel

Overchannel

  • Effect: Cast a spell even with no slots of that level remaining by paying with Spellburn: burn attribute points equal to twice the spell's level (a flat cost that doesn't double).
  • The magic tears through you regardless: you also take 1d6 unavoidable damage per spell level, and the casting always succeeds.
  • This is the Sorcerer's answer to having fewer slots than a Wizard: you're never truly out of options, just paying more for the privilege.
  • No roll required. The damage cannot be reduced by any means

10th Level — Bloodline Awakening

Bloodline Awakening

  • Effect: Your bloodline's power deepens. Gain the 10th-level ability from your Bloodline Kit.

20th Level — Sorcerer's Spark (Improved)

Sorcerer's Spark (Improved)

  • Effect: Sorcerer's Spark is now usable twice per day. Additionally, Wild Surges used during a Sorcerer's Spark don't count against your daily Wild Surge limit.

24th Level — Chaos Incarnate

Chaos Incarnate

  • Effect: Once per day, become a conduit of pure chaos: your next three spells cost no slot.
  • After the third spell the GM rolls once on the Corruption Table regardless of what happened during it — the chaos always leaves a mark

Spells Known

  • The Sorcerer's Spells Known list is their total available spell repertoire — smaller than a Wizard's spellbook, but every spell on it is always ready to cast from any matching slot. Cantrips are always available and never consume a slot.
  • Bonus Spells: Charisma 13-15 grants one extra 1st level spell known. 16-17 grants one extra 2nd level spell known. 18+ grants one extra 3rd level spell known.
  • Retraining: During a Downtime Phase, a Sorcerer may replace one spell they know with another of the same level.

Spell Progression

Fewer slots than the Wizard — the trade-off for spontaneous casting, plus Overchannel as a release valve when you run dry.

Bloodline Kits

Each kit is an item in the Kits compendium, in the Sorcerer folder. Drag one onto your character.

  • Choose one Bloodline Kit at character creation.
  • Your kit defines your magical origin and grants two abilities — a 1st-level Bloodline Ability and a powerful Bloodline Awakening at 10th level.
  • All DCs a Sorcerer imposes on a target use the standard spell-save formula (see Spellcasting in Arneyan): DC = 10 + half your Sorcerer level (minimum 1) + Charisma modifier.

Sorcerer Spell List

  • Spells available to the Sorcerer, by level. * = reversible spell. ‡ = needs a costed material component (see Rare Spell Components in the Shopkeeper's Catalogue).
  • Full descriptions, saves and components are in Spellcasting in Arneyan.
  • Includes every Wizard-list spell of the Sorcerer’s favoured schools (Evocation and Transmutation), up to the highest spell level the Sorcerer can cast, except Time Stop, Forcecage, Limited Wish, Permanency and Polymorph Any Object, plus the spells listed below.
